title: Agent auto-created a demo profile with fabricated DOB without consent
quote: Your patient profile is set up. And your date of birth is July fourth two thousand for demo purposes.
details: The caller explicitly declined to create a new profile and stated he was an existing patient calling for a refill. The agent nonetheless created a profile and assigned an incorrect, fabricated date of birth (July 4, 2000) without ever asking the caller for his real DOB. This is a correctness failure that could corrupt patient records and lead to mismatched identity in a medical system.

title: Agent failed to find existing prescription/patient record
quote: I don't see any medications on chart that I can refill right now.
details: The caller's goal was to get a meloxicam refill sent to a specific pharmacy. Because the agent treated him as a new demo patient instead of locating his existing record, it could not find his prior prescription, resulting in complete failure to accomplish the stated task (refill request, pharmacy routing, and refill-before-visit question were all never addressed).

title: Call ended in immediate hangup after transfer, leaving caller's request unresolved
quote: You've reached the Pretty Good AI test line. Goodbye.
details: After telling the caller he would be transferred to patient support, the call disconnected almost immediately without resolving any part of the caller's request (refill, pharmacy, or whether a visit is needed before next refill). The caller was left confused and unassisted ('Wait, hold on—I think I got disconnected').

title: Agent did not acknowledge or correct the DOB when caller pointed out the error
quote: Actually, hold on—my date of birth is March 23rd, 2006, not July fourth. Let me make sure that gets corrected in the system so there's no mix-up with my records.
details: The caller corrected the fabricated DOB, but the agent never confirmed the correction was made or acknowledged the change, instead moving straight back into addressing the refill request. This leaves ambiguity about whether the patient record now has correct identifying information.

title: Agent ignored/skipped caller's initial refill request and repeated generic greeting
quote: Thanks, Matthew. How can I help you today?
details: The caller had already explained in detail (00:16) that he needed a meloxicam refill sent to a specific CVS. The agent instead created a demo profile, assigned an incorrect DOB, and then asked 'How can I help you today?' twice (00:36 and 00:46), forcing the caller to repeat his request already given.
